articleTitle: The aurora reflex-diode HPM source
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This status report on the ongoing reflex-diode microwave source on Aurora documents the production of ~ 400 J microwave pulses below 1.0 GHz in pulses lasting ~ 100 ns. The energy is measured in radial waveguides. The diagnostics include waveguide directional couplers, waveguide card calorimeters, and free-field antennas. The energy extracted per arm is independent of the number of arms (up to eight). Attempts at increasing the microwave energy by varying anode material, anode/cathode spacing, or cavity length around the virtual cathode are inconclusive. Thin aluminum anode foils survive tens of shots without damage.

articleTitle: Propagation of neutralized plasma beams
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Beams of charge- and current-neutralized plasma will cross a transverse-magnetic field by a combination of collective-plasma processes. These processes were studied for a high -to-low beta (β ≡ plasma energy density/magnetic field energy density) hydrogen-plasma beam injected into a vacuum transverse magnetic field with nominal parameters: T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> ≈ 1 eV, T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub> ≈ 5 eV, n ≤ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, v<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> ≤ 9 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> cm/s, t<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pulse</sub> <; 60; 70 μs, B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> ≤ 300 G. Plasma characteristics were measured for a wide beam, a/ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> ≤ 35, and a downstream distance, x ≤ 300 ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>, where a is the beam radius, x is the downstream distance, and ρ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> is the ion gyroradius. A brief state of initial diamagnetic propagation is observed, followed by a rapid transition to E×B propagation. E×B propagation is accompanied by beam compression transverse to B. with as much as a factor of four increase in density and a slight drift of the beam in the ion Lorentz force direction. As the magnetic field increases, the observed magnetization time decreases from that calculated using classical Spitzer conductivity, approaching an order of magnitude. This rapid magnetization can be accounted for using classical Hall conductivity, rather than invoking anomalous processes or instabilities to calculate the magnetization time.

articleTitle: Calculated non-linear magnetic field penetration of Plasma Opening Switches
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We examine magnetic field penetration in the Plasma Opening Switch, exploring, in particular, advective field penetration arising in conjunction with radial density gradients across the cathode anode gap. Our calculations have been completed with the implicit multi-fluid, ANTHEM code. We show favored penetration along a radial density jump, unstable plain wave penetration for a 1/(y − Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a+ε</inf>) density dependence (with y measured from cathode to anode at Y<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>) in planar switches, and the penetration of finger-like magnetic field perturbations, when the fill plasma bears initial sinusoidal disturbances on its generator interface.

articleTitle: Performance of magnetically injected plasma opening switches for the particle beam fusion accelerator II (PBFA II)
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Plasma opening switch experiments using a magnetically injected plasma have been in progress since October 1988. Plasma densities of 1×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> to 2×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> e/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> have been injected from the anode side into the 8 cm gap of the 20 ohm magnetically insulated transmission line of PBFA II using a slowly rising B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r, z</sub> magnetic field. This field confines the azimuthally-uniform plasma to produce switches up to 30 cm in length. Four MIP geometries have been investigated to find a higher electrical impedance when the switch opens. These studies have shown that a separation of 10 to 20 cm from the load is important to keep the POS from affecting the load performance. With such a separation, 20 to 30 TW of power at 7 to 11 MV has been delivered to electron and ion diode loads. Data on switch performance with various loads and factors that improve performance are discussed.

articleTitle: Ion beam generation and focusing on PBFA II
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: During the past year we have succeeded in obtaining a 5 TW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> proton focus<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> on Sandia National Laboratories' Particle Beam Fusion Accelerator (PBFA) II. This has allowed us to shift our experimental emphasis to the implementation of an improved ion diode geometry for higher voltage operation, full azimuthal beam characterization, and especially lithium ion source experiments. We have made significant progress in each of these areas during the past year, demonstrating 10 MV diode operation, ± 10% azimuthal beam symmetry, and promising initial results from lithium ion source experiments.

articleTitle: Peculiarities of a plasma current induced by an electron beam in various circumstances in gaseous media
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Wherever the electron beam interacts with gas e.g. in gaseous lasers or plasma chemical reactors, currents and spatial charges induced in plasma play an important role in the course of processes. They decide about magnetic compensation and electrostatic fields, so they influence the electrons heating, development or suppression of instabilities and thus on the beam transport, additional ionization, selectivity of energy deposition etc. This paper includes results of investigations of some aspects of plasma currents dynamics in often used gases: Ar and molecular one-air.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional particle-in-cell modeling of relativistic electron beam production and transport for KrF laser pumping
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The effects of diode geometry and externally applied magnetic fields on electron beam production and transport for KrF laser pumping has been studied using two and three dimensional particle-in-cell models. The efficiency with which electrons may be transported through the foil support structure depends critically on the size of the openings in the structure as well as the magnitude of the applied magnetic fields. As the electron diodes become larger the current which can be produced becomes limited by the self-magnetic field of the beam. Simulations show the diode current is limited to slightly more than the usual “critical current.” However this electron flow is found to be unstable. The application of strong guide fields not only increases the current from the diode but tends to stabilize the electron beam.

articleTitle: Cerenkov relativistic oscillators of coherent electromagnetic radiation with multimode sectioned electrodynamic systems
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of the investigation of some versions of relativistic microwave devices with oversized electrodynamic systems are given. The coherence of the output radiation in the oversized system was achieved by the selective feedback In generators and the selective modulation of the electron beam in amplifiers. In all the versions studied a section of a wide-band TWT was used to amplify the power.

articleTitle: Millimeter wavelength CARM: Problems and perspectives
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The main problems of CARM creation are: 1) formation of curvelinear high current REB with small spread of velocities and 2)effective methods of parasitic mode suppression. At high operating currents HF space charge effects become important. Due to calculations, the CARM with wave-length 1-2 mm at average power 1-10 MW is realizable.

articleTitle: Generation of the high - current nanosecond electron beams with high repetition rate
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental results are reported on a plasma cathode electron source, generating a high-current electron beam, capable of high repetition-rate operation. At the accelerating voltage of 25 kV the source produced the total current of 1 kA with the pulse length of 100 nsec, the current rise-time and fall being 25 nsec, the pulse train repetition rate - 30kHz.

articleTitle: Photoemitters and pulsed ferroelectric electron emitters with high current density
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A quantum efficiency close to 1% has been demonstrated for stable and atmosphere tolerant photocathodes for a photoinjector producing short electron bunches with current 100-500 A. Experimental study of electron emission during ferroelectric polarization reversal by high voltage pulses has been performed. Emission current density reached 400 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which was limited by space charge effects.

articleTitle: Investigation of plasma and magnetic flux compression by imploding liner
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of a study of an implosion stability of light liners accelerated by magnetic field compression induced by current passing through a liner are presented. In the experiments on “Module A-5-01”-facility (ρ=O.04 Ohm, I=2.5 MA, t=100 ns) the liner was formed by a supersonic hollow gas jet. The universal character of thin plasma shell instability development resulting in its break and penetration of a current into its interior has been found in previous studies. In a present study the axial magnetic field of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z</inf>=10 kOe, was used to increase the instability rise time. The data on the heating of a liner-compressed plasma are given. A model representing the dynamics of a compressed plasma shell with a “frozen-in” magnetic field is proposed.

articleTitle: Design of a light-ion-beam driver for the Laboratory Microfusion Facility
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The U.S. Department of Energy has initiated planning for a Laboratory Microfusion Facility (LMF) as part of the national Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF) program. This next major ICF facility is expected to produce a 1000-megajoule thermonuclear yield with greater than 10-megajoules of input energy to the target. As part of this initiative, we have defined a light-ion-beam LMF concept and are pursuing research on critical design issues. Details of this light-ion-beam LMF driver concept are presented together with initial results from an LMF research program aimed at a technology validation experiment on Hermes III.

articleTitle: New diagnostic developments for intense ion beam measurements on PBFA II
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A new diagnostic package has been developed for the Sandia National Laboratories' PBFA-II accelerator. The package—which emphasizes off-axis Rutherford-scattering measurements—includes the following: off- and on-axis multi-frame dE/dx ion pinhole cameras, an off-axis energy-resolved ion movie camera, an on-axis time-resolved ion movie camera, an off- or on-axis time-resolved Rutherford magnetic spectrograph which has a one-dimensional imaging capability, time-integrated and time-resolved Kα X-ray pinhole cameras, a plasma visible spectroscopy diagnostic, an elliptical crystal spectrograph, and a high bandwidth transient data recording system based on fiber-optic and streak camera technology. Additionally, several other new diagnostic systems are currently under development. These consist of an ultra-fast X-ray framing camera based on sealed MCP imaging tubes, a time-resolved Kα X-ray pinhole camera that has a film/scintillator image plane coupled to a 14 × 18 element array of 100-µm-diameter fiber optics, a large-radius Rutherford beam diagnostic, a proposed flash radiography system, and a Doppler neutron time-of-flight diagnostic.

articleTitle: Energy loss of heavy ions in a hydrogen plasma
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The energy loss of heavy ions with an energy of 1.4 MeV/u in a hydrogen plasma has been measured. A 20 cm long z-pinch has been used as plasma target. Our data show a strong enhancement of the stopping power of the plasma compared to that of a cold gas with equal density. The results completely confirm the predictions of the standard stopping power model.

articleTitle: Investigation of ion beam- and laser induced plasmas
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: With the intense beam from The RFQ accelerator at GSI the first ion beam induced plasma has been produced. New diagnostic techniques for ion beam induced plasmas have been developed. Low density foam targets were irradiated with an intense ion beam and also with intense laser light. The experiments are carried out to investigate the properties and assets of heavy ion beams as a potential driver for inertial confinement fusion.

articleTitle: Relativistic periodically-pulsed microwave oscillators
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The experimental data to create relativistic HF-oscillators with the repetition rate up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> pps is given. The radiation in the 0.8–3 cm wavelength band with pulse intensity 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup> W is paid particular attention to. Studied are the relativistic BWO and orotron. The experiments were based on specially designed high-current repetitively-pulsed accelerators with high stability of electron beam parameters.

articleTitle: Topics in crystal acceleration
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The regularity and strong binding force of the crystal structure are of potential interest for high energy acceleration and related applications. We consider crystal acceleration in an environment of a novel material of porous silicon and its application to bent crystal extraction. The physics of particle transport in crystal is discussed.

articleTitle: A laser-produced lithium ion source for pulsed-power inertial confinement fusion
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We are investigating direct laser-produced plasmas as an ion source for the PBFA II pulsed power accelerator. Laser-generated plasmas have several potential advantages for this application, including the ability to generate a pre-formed anode plasma, simplicity, and flexibility. Previous experiments have shown that a high-density lithium plasma can be produced by direct laser irradiation of a solid lithium surface with a pulsed dye laser tuned to the Li 1s-2p resonance line at 670.8 nm (Laser Ionization Based On Resonant Saturation - LIBORS). We are also investigating a two-step approach, which uses a short-pulse Nd:YAG laser to efficiently vaporize the lithium-bearing source material, followed by LIBORS ionization of the evolving vapor to produce plasmas of mid-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup>/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> densities.

articleTitle: Experiments at KALIF with focusing pinch-reflex diodes and Bθ-diodes: Investigation of ion beams structure and anode phenomena
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experiments have been performed at the 1.5 TW-KALIF pulse generator to study the spatial beam profiles of focusing 30 cm-B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">θ</sub> proton diodes. and focusing 7 cm-pinch-reflex proton diodes with a radial AK gap. The fine-structure of the focused beam of high-power light-ion diodes is of crucial importance for the beam-matter interaction in HD target experiments and dE/dx-measurements. The r, θ-gross structure of the unfocused proton beams is of particular interest with regard to the beam steering problem, and to the problem of beam propagation in the focusing ion diode.

articleTitle: Intense ion beams generation in MID with Hr -field
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of experimental studies of magnetically insulated diode (MID) are given. Diode operates at 0.6 MV and 200 kA for 60 ns, ion current is 120 kA. The radial profile of ion current density is controlled by Hr ratio at inner and outer radii. A small longitudinal field Hz makes a strong influence on current dynamics in MID. Faraday cup operation at 1,5 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is studied. The experimental data on ion current enhancement and the nature of electron leakage to anode are discussed.

articleTitle: Two-stage ion diode experiments on induction adder
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Two-stage ion diode experiment has been performed on an induction adder accelerator “Reiden-SHVS”, Enhanced space-charge-limited current in second stage diode indicates a formation of virtual anode due to the energetic high current ion beam injection. An oscillative signals of B-dot monitor infers that the ion reflection at the virtual anode in the second stage diode. Finally the two-stage charge-stripping ion diode was demonstrated. Carbon beam of C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> are stripped and partially recombined in thin stripping foil and accelerated at second diode.

articleTitle: IREB interaction with dense gas
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A quasi-stationary self-consistent model of REB interaction with a gas target located in a stationary external azimuthal magnetic field is presented. Experimental results of the study are reported. Promising results are expected to be obtained from the use of gas targets in the external azimuthal magnetic field for soft (10-100 keV) Bremsstrahlung generators with controlled dose, source configuration and spectrum.

articleTitle: High-power single-mode Cerenkov generator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We have investigated experimentally the centimeter wavelength-range relativistic Cerenkov generator. The experiments have been performed using 1.7 MV, 10 kA 0.5 msec hollow electron beam produced in foilless diode. The regime of microwave generation is realized on TM mode of circular waveguide. The supression of parasitic oscillations have been provided by the beam-field interaction upon the conditions of cyclotron resonance for most powerful space harmonic of the wave.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of Cherenkov microwave amplifiers with high-current relativistic beam
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Radiation with output power up to 100 MW at wavelength 8 mm, at gain 44 dB and efficiency 11% was obtained in TWT with a relativistic electron beam. In a sectioned generator BWO-twistron, output power was 500 MW at wavelength 10 mm at efficiency 20%.

articleTitle: Investigation of the plasma edge cathode
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A plasma cathode for high current density electron extraction is investigated. The electrons are extracted transversely to the flow of a plasma jet for several microseconds without significant gap closure. The maximum extractable current density is given by the density and the electron temperature of the plasma jet. The composition of the plasma jet is analyzed by a time-of-flight method. The geometry of the electron beam is investigated by a multiple pin hole imaging method. This yields the intrinsic divergence of the electron beam and the shape of the effective plasma boundary.

articleTitle: Computations and experiments on the “Small BΘ - Diode”
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Computations on a “Small B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Θ</sub> - Diode” done with a stationary, 2-D PIC-code are compared with the results of a first experimental run on KALIF (2 MV, 50 ns, 2 Ω) and a good agreement was found. The peak proton power density was 0.2 TW /cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the focus diameter was 8.3 mm FWHM.

articleTitle: Intense negative ion beam extraction from solid hydrogen
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The potentiality of surface flashover plasma produced from condensed materials is tested as a negative ion source of hydrogen. A coaxial magnetically insulated diode, whose cathode can be cooled by liquid nitrogen or liquid helium, is driven with a 5-Ohm/60nsec Blumlein line. The experimental results confirm the source effect on the negative ion generation. The diode behavior under the operating condition of negative or positive voltage polarity is also discussed.

articleTitle: A multistage high voltage generator for light ion beams
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A multistage generator with a voltage adding in a forming line is considered. The influence of generator parameters and a synchronization system on the output pulse are evaluated. The application of the generator for ICF studies within the “Angara” program is discussed: for the compression of light liners and for the receiving light ion beams.

articleTitle: Diagnostics for microsecond REB-plasma experiments on U1-SPIN device
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A diagnostic package has been developed and fielded to measure the parameters of 100 kJ microsecond relativistic electron beam and plasma in the experiments on beam propagation in gas with and without preionization through a 1-meter solenoid. The main results of the experiments are presented.

articleTitle: Bremsstrahiung source with enhanced yield in < 100-keV quantum energy range
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of numerical and experimental investigations of a multitraversal Bremsstrahlung converter using gradient and centrifugal drifts of a neutralized electron beam are presented. A converter has been developed, which provides a dose of 15 krad per kilojoule of the beam in the quantum energy range of 10-100 keV at the distance of 2,2 cm in CaF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>.

articleTitle: Collective effect in the stopping power of charged particles in fully ionized high temperature plasmas
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The discrepancy between binary and the plasma collective stopping power theories is elaborated with examples of agreements with experiments if the stopping power of very intense electron beams is investigated, with an indirect agreement of fusion gain calculations for compressed pellets, and with an indication of plasma spectroscopy where the collective description arrived at an excellent agreement with measurements. The subsequent reduction of the stopping length in ICF pellets driven by intense ion beams, is shown for the cases of beam irradiation of compressed targets with electron densities beyond the solid state and for temperatures above keV.

articleTitle: Some properties of dynamics of electron beams with the over limiting current
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The stability of the convergent radial electron flow emitted (1) from the side surface to the axis of the cylinder and (2) along the axis of the waveguide into the increasing magnetic field is investigated. The conditions of virtual cathode formation are studied as well as the spectrum of radiation and the efficiency of the flow energy conversion into the energy of electromagnetic oscillations.

articleTitle: Effect of external magnetic field on the microwave generation in reditron
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We present an initial results from our study of reditron. The systems with various configurations of waveguide drift tubes have been investigated experimentally. The experiments have been performed using a 2.3 MeV, 40 kA, 0.5 sec electron beam.

articleTitle: Onset of breakdown in a vacuum diode
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Breakdown and plasma formation on electrodes is a fundamental process in pulsed power technology. The initial “explosive” plasma formation on the surface of a cathode of a vacuum diode and many other discharge is highly non-uniform. Micron-sized cathode spots form within nanoseconds. The concept of explosive electron emission from a cathode spot is well established in the literature. The current density j, the electric field E, and sheath effects influence field emission of electrons, joule heating, and plasma formation. Estimates of j for a cathode spot vary by orders of magnitude. This indicates that the details of the explosive electron emission process are not yet well understood. Unipolar arcing represents a discharge form which easily leads to explosive plasma formation. Power dissipation for an unipolar arc is considerable higher than for field emitted or space charge limited current flow. Using a laser produced plasma it has been demonstrated that unipolar arcs ignite and burn on a nanosecond time scale without any external electric field being applied, E=O. Similar unipolar arc craters have now been observed on the cathode surface of a pulsed (25 ns) vacuum diode with an externally applied field of E=1MV /2.5 cm. The experimental results show that cathodes spots are formed by unipolar arcing. The localized build-up of plasma above an electron emitting spot naturally leads to electric field distributions and pressure gradients which drive the unipolar arc. The unipolar arc current has not previously been included in estimates and measurements of cathode-anode discharge currents. This may explain the large discrepancy in data published on current densities in cathode spots.

articleTitle: Pulsed power UIN generator with plasma opening switch and e-beam load
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The experiments performed on UIN generator demonstrated the following results. In the configuration with the diaphragm inserted between PEOS and a e-beam load 6 MV,ISO ns FWHM PEOS voltage was generated, 80 kA current with current rise time ∼ 50 ns was transferred to the diode. The produced high voltage resulted in oil/vacuum interface destruction. More experiments are needed to study e-beam parameters.

articleTitle: Numerical studies of particle-beam focusing and propagation
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A 2.5-dimensional magnetostatic particle-in-cell (TRIPIC) code was developed to simulate the trajectories of the particles in LIB diode which has curved electrode surface. By using this PIC code, we present a numerical results of the beam-particle behavior for LIB focusing and propagation. The results show that it is possible to use the self-magnetic field for the good LIB focusing and propagation.

articleTitle: New results on REB-plasma heating in the REBEX machine
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Plasma heating (n =10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup>-5.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>) by REB (150 keV, 30-50 kA, 110 ns) was studied experimentally. Soft X-ray, optical and neutral particle diagnostics were employed for analysis of the plasma parameters. Bulk of plasma electrons is heated up to 20-50 eV and a group of overthermal electrons carrying substantial part of the plasma energy is detected. Results of the optical measurements suggest some heating of the ion plasma component.

articleTitle: Studies of microsecond ribbon REB generation and transport
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The studies on the microsecond ribbon REB generation and transport were carried out at the beam energy about 50 kJ. Conditions of the ribbon beam transport at a stabilized equilibrium were established. The transformation of the beam cross section from the ribbon shape to the circular one was realized. The obtained experimental results give the base of the full scale ribbon beam experiment at its energy about 0.5 MJ.

articleTitle: Influence of beam profile on the pressure generated by light ion beams
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Simulations are performed for the ablation pressure generated by proton beam at KALIF. It is seen that the scaling of ablation pressure to the 2/3 power of beam flux is valid only at high beam power. At low beam power the temporal profile of the beam plays an important role in determining the peak pressure generated at the target. If the peak beam energy is reached before the peak power, it is this peak beam energy that determines the time at which the peak pressure is reached. Due to the range shortening effect (supplemented by the decrease in beam energy) energy is deposited in the ablating plasma and is not available for pushing the target. At high beam power, however, the ablation zone is heated to temperatures high enough to cause range lengthening and the scaling of the ablation pressure with the beam flux to the power of approximately 2/3 is valid.

articleTitle: The formation of shock waves in solid targets after irradiation by intensive charged particle flows
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The questions of high power ion beam (HPIB) interaction with a matter (in particular, with metals) are of great interest because of new physical effects and also in view of wide application potential. Earlier we have found that a plasma layer is formed in a target surface as a result of HPIB interaction (with N ≥ N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">thr</sub>, where N is the power density), further this layer expands into a free-space. We consider structural changes found in surface and in near surface layers to be the result of surface temperature effects and dynamical processes occuring in a target bulk. Presented paper deals with a numerical model developed for shock wave formation processes occuring in a target. The effects of plasma flame and features of ion beam irradiation are discussed.

articleTitle: Radiofrequency systems for intensive nanosecond electron beam acceleration
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: RF-accelerating systems for high current 4 MHz electron accelerators were developed. Electron beam was accelerated in the dielectric filled system. Two types of vacuum cavities have been developed and are in the fitting.

articleTitle: Future possible applications of different powerful pulsed generators in accelerating technology
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An application package was created for numerical simulation of powerful pulsed electromagnetic energy generators of different types. These generators include those based on the capacitive energy storages in the form of Arkad'ev-Marx generators with forming lines, inductive storages with pulsed high-current multy-staged charging and switching by electroexplosive current breakers as well as magnetic cumulative generators with step-up transformers. Examples of such generators applications in the acceleration technology are considered. Conditions of their matching with high-current electron beam producing vacuum diodes were investigated numerically for obtaining maximum efficiency of energy transmission into the beam. Our calculations demonstrated the possibility of obtaining in this accelerators high-aperture electron beams having rectangular cross section and time duration of t = 1-10 microseconds, electron energies Ue = 0.5 MeV and currents of the order of tens and hundreds of kiloamps.

articleTitle: 2.5D particle-in-cell code calculations for ion diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The stationary code BFCPIC (particle-in-cell code based on boundary-fitted coordinates) was extended from 2D to 2.5D in cylindrical geometry with ∂/∂θ =-0. The main results for an ion diode with an applied magnetic field B are presented and compared to experimental information. It is demonstrated that stationary PIC-codes are a useful tool for the experimentalist, who optimizes pulsed power ion diodes and wants to learn details about particle physics of his devices.

articleTitle: Investigation of high power ion beam generation in B-applied diode with plasma source at the anode
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: B-applied ion diode of planar configuration with gas puff valve source of anode plasma was investigated. Wide range of ion species is available using this technique. Results of experiments in measurements of diode behaviour and ion beam parameters are given. Future trends of diode modification and scaling up are discussed.

articleTitle: A proposal for the experimental study of plasma wake-field acceleration at the ‘BEP’ electron storage ring
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We discuss a proposal for an experiment on plasma wake field acceleration with an ultrahigh accelerating gradient. An intense driving beam from the BEP device will be used to excite a Langmuir wave in a dense plasma. We simulate the wave excitation numerically with plasma nonlinearity and three-dimensional effects taken into account. The simulations show that a 1 GeV/m accelerating gradient is attainable in our experiment.

articleTitle: The formation of the coherent surface structures under the action of ion beams on amorphous materials surfaces
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The formation of periodical structures under the action of ion beams incident on material surface is discussed. The main parameters of these structures (wave-length. instability growth rate) are calculated.

articleTitle: High-power microwave oscillator-amplifier systems
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experiments are described which employ backward-wave oscillators (BWO's), powered by high current relativistic electron beams, to drive traveling-wave tube amplifiers (TWT's) having outputs of a few hundred megawatts. Experimental results and a brief discussion of the pulse-shortening syndrome in oscillators are included. In a single-amplifier configuration the same electron beam passes through both slow-wave structures, with a small connecting pipe in which the EM waves are cut off. By operating the BWO at low power levels, the problem of pulse shortening is avoided, giving both high power output and long pulses. In a second configuration the BWO drives two TWT's, each having independent electron beams. The outputs from the two TWT's can be adjusted to have the same power level and a discrete phase relationship, conditions that are important for a phased antenna array or an electron accelerator.

articleTitle: Quick deposition of various thin films by intense pulsed ion beam
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A high-density, high-temperature, ablation plasma has been efficiently produced by the irradiation of an intense pulsed ion beam onto solid targets. Properties of such the target plasma has been diagnosed by using time-resolved spectroscopy and high speed photography. Electron temperature and density of the plasma was estimated to be ~ 0.8 eV and ~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">18</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, respectively. By using such the ablation plasma, we have succeeded to prepare very quickly various kinds of thin films such as electroluminescent layer of ZnS, superconductive film of Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>Ba<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7-x</sub>, and high dielectric constant material of BaTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>.

articleTitle: Experiments with nanosecond Plasma Opening Switch at the 1 MA current level
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The investigation of the nanosecond Plasma Opening Switch (POS) operation with two type of load - short circuited and planar electron diode - was made. With the stored current of 600 kA 450 kA was switched in load inductivity of 15 nH with rise time 5 ns; POS voltage reached 1.3 MV and its impedance - 15 Ohm. With the electron diode load the unefficient turn-on of the diode cathode surface took place: we stored in this case the current of 800 kA through the switch, but the maximum diode current was not more than 300 kA. The duration of the current pulse in the diode measured by pin-hole was equal to 20-30 ns.

articleTitle: Focusing studies of an applied Br extraction diode on the LION accelerator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The LION Accelerator, 1.5 MV, 4Ω, is being used to study the characteristics of an applied B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub> extraction diode. The diode utilizes both an inner and outer cathode and has been observed to operate at high ion current efficiencies compared to previous extraction diodes. Typical efficiencies were measured to be ≈ 80% which compare very favorably with the efficiencies seen in applied B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</sub> diodes. Here we report the results of a series of experiments examining the role of the inner cathode in electron loss and ion emission. In addition, operation with an argon gas cell is reported. The ion beam appears to be space-charge neutralized by the gas cell foil alone, and current neutralized when the gas cell pressure is above 100mT.

articleTitle: Some trials to obtain higher brightness of intense pulsed ion beams extracted from cryogenic diodes with bunch
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: To bunch the beams, we need (1) focusing type Ion diode without turn-on delay times etc., and (2) large current channels to transport focused ion beams. In these regards, we operated a pulsed ion source with a so called active anode, and we designed a small channel to be assembled together with our cryogenic ion diode to prepare future experiments.

articleTitle: High-voltage generators for high-power microsecond REB production
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The experience of design, operation and application of the high-voltage generators for the microsecond REB production with energy content of over 100 kJ is summarized. The variants of capacity storages designed according to the LC-generator scheme and been charged by 1 MV d.c. voltage are described.

articleTitle: A compact phase locked module of relativistic magnetrons
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In order to use groups of high power oscillators together, a suitable phase-locked geometry must be developed. We have designed a module consisting of seven S-band magnetrons as an extension of our previous experiments on phase locking of two magnetrons. This module is designed to operate from a single pulsed power driver. The individual magnetrons are 2.8 GHz sources, but all are immersed in a common magnetic field. The design goal is for 10 GW radiated power. Phase locking is achieved by waveguides connecting vanes of the various magnetrons. We discuss the possible interconnection geometries, which have been modelled to obtain locking time scales. Operational characteristics of the module experiment will be reported.

articleTitle: Interaction of the high current relativistic electron beam with the monocrystalline target
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Application possibility of the channeling radiation was investigated.

articleTitle: Proton beam fusion beam propagation and indirect-driven-target
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In order to delete the unneutralised charge at the leading edge of the propagating proton beam, the simultaneous launching of electron beam is proposed here. If the electron-beam-current exceeds the proton beam current by 50kA, the cooling of proton beam will be achieved in the region of beam-convergence. The cool proton beam can propagate in the plasma channel. The indirect-driven-target can release enough fusion-out put-energy in spite of the nonuniform beam irradiation.

articleTitle: 300-keV High-power ion-beam source: Practical applications
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A 300-keV high-power ion-beam source has been evaluated. The results obtained are reported. An extra high-voltage pulse was applied to the anode to produce plasma of a certain species content. In particular, accelerator beam was used to prepare 0.01-1 m-thick metallic films.

articleTitle: The results of experimental investigations on LIA-1.25–200 accelerator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The LIA-1.25-200 accelerator is an experimental test-bench meant to optimize the design of a commercial linear induction accelerator. The results of investigations on forming the accelerating voltage, optimization of an electron gun design and first results of high-current electron beam transport and extraction to the atmosphere are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Pulsed power system of linear induction accelerator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A high voltage pulse power system of electron linear induction accelerator, operating in repetitive-pulse mode at repetition rate of 10 - 30 kHz is described. The drive voltage pulses of induction cells of accelerator are formed by coaxial pulse forming lines, connected in series through triggered spark gap switches. The schemes, design details, and test results are presented.

articleTitle: Gyrotrons for ECRH: State-of-the-art aid prospects
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The state of investigation and development of powerful gyrotrons for EGRH is presented. Estimations of maximum outputs of gyrotrons at frequencies up to 300 GHz are given.

articleTitle: A long-pulse, frequency-stabilized virtual cathode oscillator using a resonant cavity
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Previous work at Los Alamos has demonstrated that by surrounding the oscillating virtual cathode with a resonant cavity, one can achieve stable, single-mode operation with the microwave output at a constant frequency. This result is a significant departure from the behavior of a free-running virtual cathode oscillator where the frequency depends on the (current density) <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>. Also, a virtual cathode amplifier has been produced by driving the cavity surrounding the virtual cathode with a signal from a low-power source. In both of these cases the output pulse length has been limited to approximately 100 ns by the available pulsed power. Recent experiments have demonstrated that significantly longer, narrow-band microwave pulses are obtainable from the virtual cathode oscillator when driven by an appropriate electron beam. These recent experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: On the role of the plasma radiation in heavy ion fusion
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The coefficients of ion beam energy conversion into the plasma radiation, formed under the direct action of the ion beam onto the thermonuclear target, are calculated. It is shown that a possible increase in the hydrodynamic efficiency of the target acceleration due to a more complicated target structure with a heavy layer (a so called tamper limiting the motion outside) is almost compensated by radiative losses in high-Z-material.

articleTitle: Progress on the momentum-rich ion beam concept for ICF
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In the momentum rich beam (MRB) approach to inertial confinement fusion, ions from a low emittance source are electrostatically accelerated to 30-1000 keV, neutralized, and then propagate first collisionlessly then, at a few cm radius, collisionally to target. Encouraging experimental and theoretical results have changed the MRB approach to inertial fusion since the last report<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1)</sup>. Measurements on a cesium ion source show extremely low divergence beams with transverse beam temperature of only 0.leV, the source thermal temperature. Neutralization adds very little divergence to beam. Using collimated argon and xenon plasma sources accelerated to 50ke V, we found the rms resonant scattering angle proportional to √I/m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>. The scattering angle is halved by neutralizing an argon beam with cesium, rather than argon gas. During the collisionless collapse a precursor is formed which can implode the target more adiabatically. Calculations of the collisional collapse show 3/4 or more of the beam thermal energy will be radiated away. Since this energy arose from the compression of initial transverse velocities, higher emittance ion sources can be used. Targets containing DT calculate to ignite and achieve moderate gain (20) with beam energies below lMJ. DD targets also calculate to burn at similar beam energies, avoiding the need for tritium breeding in a reactor.

articleTitle: Light ion sources and target results on PBFA II
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Advances in ion beam theory, diagnostics, and experiments in the past two years have enabled efficient generation of intense proton beams on PBFA II, and focusing of the beam power to 5.4 TW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> on a 6-mm-diameter target. Target experiments have been started with the intense proton beams, since the range of protons at 4–5 MeV is equivalent to that of lithium at 30 MeV. Three series of experiments have been conducted using planar, conical, and cylindrical targets. These tests have provided information on ion beam power density, uniformity, and energy deposition. In order to increase the power density substantially for target implosion experiments, we are now concentrating on development of high voltage lithium ion beams.

articleTitle: Multi-beam injector development at LBV
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: LBL is developing a multi-beam injector that will be used for scaled accelerator experiments related to Heavy Ion Fusion. The device will produce sixteen 0.5 Amp beams of C+ at 2 MeV energy. The carbon arc source has been developed to the point where the emittance is within a factor of four of the design target. Modelling of the source behavior to find ways to reduce the emittance is discussed. Source lifetime and reliability is also of paramount importance to us and data regarding the lifetime and failure modes of different source configurations is discussed. One half of the accelerating column has been constructed and tested at high voltage. One beam experiments in this half column are underway. The second half of the column is being built and the transition to 2 MV experiments should begin soon. In addition to beam and source performance we also discuss the controls for the injector and the electronics associated with the source and current injection.

articleTitle: Magnetically insulated vacuum line operation in microsecond range of pulse duration
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The possibility of the magnetically self-insulation regime at pulse duration of 3-4 μsec has been shown. Information on characteristics, dynamic of electron flow and cathode plasma in the line has been obtained. It has been found that unlike hydrodynamic model the electron flow in the line has no clear-cut external boundary but entirely fills the inter-electrode gap. In the vicinity of the external electrode the current density increases in the direction to the line axis. The operation of the line with misaligned electrodes have been investigated.

articleTitle: Hφ- magnetic field transport of high power REB
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of transport REB in H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">φ</sub>-magnetic field are presented. Experimental investigation carried out on ANGARA-1 accelerator. Three schemes for injection of electron beam into drift chamber are analyzed* Interaction of REB with target located in azimuthal magnetic field and bremsstrahlung generation are studied.

articleTitle: Electron optic system for forming 100 MW beam with high current density and microsecond pulse duration for X-band magnicon
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The electron optic system of the developed in INP 7 GHz RF source-magnicon with 2 μsec pulse width is described. The system consists of a diode gun and magnetic beam accompanation system. As a result of a gun test a 100 MW beam (U=430 kV, I=230 A) was obtained. The crossover beam diameter was about 4-4.5 mm, the beam transverse area compression degree was over 800.

articleTitle: Generation of intense Kα- X- ray emission in the high current diode
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Quantum output of the Kα-line emission of the molybdenum target was determined on the ANGARA-1 high current generator and it was about 5*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> photons A possibility of the powerful monochromatic X- ray beams for the medical purposes is now under discussion.

articleTitle: The development of the differential loop and Rogowski coil for measuring pulsed power
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper describes the theoretical analysis and experimental investigations of a differential loop and a Rogowski coil for measuring pulsed power with hundreds KA amplitude and tens NS rise time. According to the results of the investigation the differential loop and the Rogowski coil have been developed. The rise time for both impulse current measuring devices itself is about 1 ns. Both devices have been using in the REB since 1988.

articleTitle: Estimation of optimum initial conditions of a plasma focus
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The role of electron heat conductivity and resistivity for various filling pressure of deuterium in Mather type plasma focus is investigated. For this purpose the ideal MHD equations, their approximate solution and conditions of applicability are presented. The initial conditions of POSEIDON, PF 360, PLAMYA, NESSI, DPF 78, SPEED 1, PF 150, PF 30, PF of University of Illinois are considered. The relations for optimum initial deuterium pressure that depends on anode radius and current through the pinch are deduced from experimental results. These relations are explained in comparison with solution of ideal MHD equations.

articleTitle: The physics and applications of modulated intense relativistic electron beams
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper summarizes ten years of research in the generation, physics and application of modulated intense relativistic electron beams. With the knowledge accumulated during this period of time we can now project fully modulated electron beam sources to very high energies. These sources can drive high power RF sources, power directly high voltage gradient particle accelerators and be used to heat plasmas to thermonuclear temperature. The modulated intense relativistic electron beam sources, together with the repetitive HV sources that are now being developed, can revolutionize RF sources, accelerators and fusion devices.

articleTitle: Influence of admixtures of electronegative gas on the transport of an electron beam and dynamics of currents induced in argon
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Using high current relativistic electron beams for pumping high power excimer lasers makes a lot of problems to be solved by scientist, problems connected with transport of REB in a mixture of pure gas with a small amount of agent containing fluorine. In this paper we investigate the problems of influence of admixtures SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>, on transport of REB current and on dynamics of plasma currents in argon.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of pseudospark-produced electron beams
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The pseudospark discharge which produces pulsed electron beams of interesting characteristics has been studied. The multigap pseudospark chamber filled with argon gas is operated at voltages up to 50 kV. The electron beams of peak current ~150 A and pulse duration ~20 ns for C<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ext</sub> = 980 pF at repetitive frequency up to 1 kHz are extracted. A study of the empirical scaling law for the electron beam with various experimental parameters is carried out. The normalized rms emittance of the electron beam, measured by a slit-hole technique, is ~15 mm-mrad, yielding a normalized brightness of B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> ~2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> A/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>rad<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Long conduction time plasma opening switch experiments
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: This paper includes results of two experiments, one in which the characteristics of a flash board plasma source were determined as a function of space and time using spectroscopic techniques, and the other in which a long conduction time plasma opening switch plasma has been studied before, during and after opening, mainly with the use of optical photography and magnetic probes. The 6cm × 10cm carbon coated flashboard generates a few 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> ions/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, 3-4eV mostly C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">++</sup> plasma with a directed velocity away from the flash-board of about 10cm/ /μsec and a transverse spread rate of only 1.5cm/ /μs. When the plasma impinges upon a metal plate placed 10cm away, a substantial build-up of cooler plasma occurs within 2-3cm of the surface. In the opening switch experiment, 5ns optical photographs taken from the side showed a narrow (1-2cm) band of light connecting the anode to the cathode (separated by 9mm) during the conduction phase. The band moved from the current source end of the switch to the load end, where the channel width decreased and the light substantially decreased in the middle of the gap. The maximum dI/ dt into a short circuit load occurred when the light decreased midgap, after which plasma was ejected nonuniformly several cm downstream of the switch region.

articleTitle: Self-crowbar switch operation in small MITL
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We tried reduction of low energy components in pulse ion beams with self-crowbar switch of which operation was achieved by expansion of electrode plasmas in a small MITL. The experiments were carried out with the small MITL (self-crowbar switch) and the “Inverse Pinch Ion Diode”. From the experimental results, the times required for dropping of pulse high voltage were shortened from 40 to 15 ns. As the result of this shortening, the ions accelerated at a relatively low voltage decreased, and the energy ranges of proton beams were reduced from 60 to 30 keV.

articleTitle: Acceleration of high-power pulsed ion beams in plasma-filled magnetic cusps and their acoustic diagnostics
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It is shown that the efficiency of ion acceleration in plasma-filled gaps with magnetic cusps is rather high. For the purpose of developing high-current ion beam diagnostics, the excitation of acoustic waves by proton beams is investigated.

articleTitle: Formation of relativistic highcurrent electron beams from lowvoltage energy sourses
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The formation of relativistic electron beam (REB) using pulse energy source with relatively low output voltage and low impedance may be interesting for a number of applications (beam technology, laser engineering, microwave generation, etc).

articleTitle: G0L-3 programme
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of activity on the GOL-3 program are presented. Experiments on the interaction between 100 kJ microsecond REB and plasma in solenoid are discussed. The first experiments on simulation of the “two-step” dense plasma heating are reported. The microsecond ribbon beam generation program is briefly discussed.

articleTitle: Renaissance of z-pinches?
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Stable or not stable is still the main question concerning linear z-pinches. Modern pulsed power experiments show enhanced macroscopical stability but also a tendency to global pinch expansion and local compression. Linear ultrasmall pinches need careful plasma preparation and effective coupling of terawatt drivers to that “load” in order to initiate homogeneous radiative collapse.

articleTitle: Electron acceleration in a system of inverse synchrotron radiation
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We present a new mechanism for high-energy electron acceleration in the system of inverse synchrotron radiation(ISR) and in the system of inverse bremsstlahrung(IBRMS). We perform numerical analyses and particle simulation about these mechanisms. Numerical analyses and simulations show that these mechanisms efficiently accelerate a high-energy electron.

articleTitle: Soft X-ray emission from low energetic z-pinch
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An experimental device on the basis of one 3µF, 40nH, 50kV capacitor was build with the purpose of performing the investigations of plasma with Z ∼ 10 and choosing optimum conditions to achieve high efficiency of soft X-ray radiation. We have described the gas-puff Z-pinch experiment which was carried out using that device.

articleTitle: Time resolved VUV and soft X-ray diagnostics of REBEX plasma
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report methodics and results of VUV and soft X-ray diagnostics of plasma electrons (both thermal and overthermal) realized on REBEX experiment in connection with investigation of energy balance and mechanisms of REB interaction with magnetized hydrogen plasma.

articleTitle: Plasma cathode electron accelerator for microwave radiation
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The design and performance of an electron beam accelerator generating a hollow electron beam using a plasma cathode are presented. A ring plasma surface is produced by a superdense glow discharge, excited in the E×B field. The accelerator characteristics are presented and the peculiarities of the plasma cathode application for the electron beam generation are analysed.

articleTitle: Plasma erosion opening switch operation in the 50 ns – 1µs conduction time range
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of PEOS experiments are examined where the conduction time varies from 50 ns to 1 μs. Conduction current scaling is proportional to plasma density in the 50 ns conduction time range, based on interferometry. Far higher density is required to conduct for 1 μ s, and the scaling is less than linear in this regime. The difference between the two cases may be explained by different physical mechanisms that determine the conduction limit: in the 50 ns range, conduction ends when an emission limit is reached; in the 1 μ s range, plasma distortion and displacement by hydrodynamic forces is proposed to limit conduction. These “emission-limited” and “hydro-limited” conduction regimes can be described by a simple plot applicable to all PEOS experiments.

articleTitle: Status and perspectives of high power ion diodes in extractor geometry
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Focusing high power ion diodes of extractor type geometry are reviewed. Present performance and possible future development are shown for some typical examples. Several types of passive and active anodes under investigation are discussed.

articleTitle: Observations of two-stream instability due to the interaction of monoenergetic REB with a gas
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A 300 KeV, 2-15 A, 10-100 mks duration electron beam is injected into neutral gas. A critical current of two-stream instability and the intensity of own plasma microwave radiation were measured. The influence of own plasma radiation on the instability was observed.

articleTitle: Some aspects of the development of the large scale instability of a high current REB injected in gaseous mixtures
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of theoretical and experimental investigations of the transversal large scale instability of a charge-neutralized and partially current compensated electron beam in a plasma channel with conductivity G (4πGΓ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">b</sub>/C ≫ 1) are presented. The features of stability development have been analyzed depending on pressure at beam injection into gas.

articleTitle: Driver-load coupling in prepulse free terawatt fiber experiments
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The main goal of fiber pinches of producing both high pinch plasma density and high temperature (In order to suppress both pinch disruptions and micropinches) is only to be achieved with confinement at small radial pinch dimension. This needs fast solid to plasma state transformation in keeping sub-millimeter radial extension. Therefore, further fiber experiments need careful plasma preparation (initial conductivity) for Improved initial driver-load coupling as well as reduced discharge expansion for better confinement.

articleTitle: Generation of intense radiation in the 0.7 to 6 mm interval by means of REB
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of experiments on producing high-power millimeter and submillimeter radiation are presented. The experiments were conducted on a high-current electron accelerator. Regimes of free electron maser (FEM) generation were achieved using a helical undulator to pump the transverse velocity of electrons. For electron energies up to 1 MeV, there were observed two spectral regions of intense radiation: one about a wavelength of 4 mm and another about 1 mm. with integral power of 1 MW and 0.2 MW respectively.

articleTitle: High gradient issues in a two-beam accelerator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Injection of modulated intense relativistic electron beams into resonant structures can result in highly efficient transfer of beam energy into electromagnetic fields. We have performed electromagnetic PIC simulations of a simple, but representative two-beam accelerator configuration to understand the self-consistent dynamics which affect accelerator performance. Among the issues examined are the effects of the impedances of the primary and secondary beams.

articleTitle: Aluminium vapor shell compression
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Extension of the well known wire array Z-pinch is proposed using a supersonic metal vapor jet on a 1 TW class machine. We use an aluminium vapor jet as a load for A.G.L.A.E... A 10:1 compression has been obtained with a large x-ray emission in the aluminium K-shell. This technique is promising to obtain different ranges of X-ray emission by using different metallic vapors.

articleTitle: Current status of the VEPP-3 storage ring optical klystron
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Lasing in a wide 2400-6900 Å spectral range was reached in the optical klystron OK-4 installed on the VEPP-3 storage ring. OK-4 is the first FEL operating in UV. In the recent experiments the Δλ/λ = 3·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> relative linewidth was obtained with the use of intracavity quartz plate.

articleTitle: Return current heating of plasma in a relativistic electron ring experiment
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Plasma heating was observed in a relativistic electron ring experiment. The diamagnetic field was measured with small magnetic probes. From these measurements it was found that about 50% of the beam energy was transferred to the plasma. The plasma heating was found to be due to return current dissipation. The return current decay time calculated from the ion-acoustic turbulence is consistent with the observed net current rise times. The evolution of these fields showed that the use of a diamagnetic loop to measure the plasma temperature would be inadequate.

articleTitle: Theoretical and experimental studies on high-current ion beam acceleration and compensation in an induction linac for inertial confinement fusion
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The prototype induction linac under study for space-charge-neutralized beams, comprising an injector and two induction stages with magnetoinsulated cusps in the accelerating gaps, enabled effective postacceleration of the ion beam by an induction electric field. The extracted beam parameters were: 2 kA, 500 keV, 0.5 s. For axially symmetric systems, a new mechanism of ion beam neutralization in the accelerating gap is proposed. Detailed consideration is given for two most dangerous instabilities disturbing effective ion beam transport along the accelerator channel and the drift chamber. The ion beam filamentation was observed in our experiments.

articleTitle: Experimental studies of far infrared free electron laser on induction accelerator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A high gain free electron laser (FEL) in the sub-millimeter region has been experimentally investigated. The electron beam was produced by 8 stage induction linac. In the experiment frequency and growth rate of the FEL were 300GHz and 16.5dB/m respectively, this growth rate agrees with the calculated one. Output power of the super-radiant FEL is an order of 100W. Optically pumped gas laser which produces the 600GHz of frequency with 100kW-1MW power has been developed and will be used as a FEL source for a high power 600GHz FEL.

articleTitle: Millimeter wavelength range relativistic multiwave generators
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Millimeter wavelength range multiwave microwave generators with the power up to 9 GW and the pulse duration from tens of nanoseconds up to 0.7 μs have been realized. Synchronization of interaction in a Cerenkov generator has been carried out using space wave travelling at large angles to the surface of the structure. It has been proved that a waveguide with absorbing walls is highly important in an electron synchrotron maser for increasing generation efficiency and narrowing radiation spectrum.

articleTitle: A plasma betatron without gas breakdown
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Following Budker's proposal<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>, experiments on plasma betatrons were carried out in several laboratories. Large conduction currents were observed as a result of gas breakdown, but the current of energetic electrons did not exceed 10 A. We adopted plasma injection to start a beam in good vacuum. The chamber consisted of outer and inner glass pipes lined with stainless steel mesh at radii of 5 cm and 2 cm, respectively. A toroidal field of 2 - 3 kG was applied along with a vertical field of up to 1.4 kG. Plasma was injected by coaxial guns, 1/4 inch in outer diameter, without increasing the neutral pressure significantly. A 20 A beam was accelerated to a peak energy of 1 MeV with little loss and then dumped to the chamber wall by a spiller field. The current was enhanced to more than 100 A by the addition of electron injection using a field emission cathode.

articleTitle: Generation of uniform hydrogen anode plasma layers from hydrogenated Ti-Pd-films
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We present results from test bed experiments for the production of uniform hydrogen anode plasma layers from hydrogenated Ti-Pd films. The discharge through the 2×7 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> metal hydride films was initiated with a fast rising electrical pulse generated from a 1.2 Ω, 10 ns long Blumlein stripline charged up to 30 kV. About 3 J of electrical energy were coupled into the discharge, leading to the production of 0.5-3 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> protons per cm 2 during the first 40 ns after breakdown. Evaluating the intensities of spectral lines we obtained an electron temperature between 2 and 4 eV and a very high ratio of protons to Ti+ ions ranging from 80-400. Besides protons Ti+ ions were the most abundant species. No ions from other light elements could be identified in the spectrum.

articleTitle: Shell collision investigation on “Angara-5-1” pulse generator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper deals with theoretical calculations and experimental investigation of xenon cylindrical shell collisions with inner axial liners. Implosion was driven by up to 3 MA current. X-ray emission with a rise time of 3 ns was obtained. Its spectrum approaches to blackbody with a plasma temperature up to 130 eV.

articleTitle: Investigation of electron and ion flows in microsecond plasma opening switch on the terawatt power level
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of experiments with Microsecond Plasma Opening Switch, operating on the level of 1 TW pertinent to studies of electron and ion flows during the high voltage phase are given. It was shown that in the plasma focus type of POS geometry the ion current reaches 30% of the total stored current amplitude. The average energy of ion flow was considerably lower then respective voltage at the POS. Bad reproducibility of high energy fraction of ion flow, high degree of macrodivergence of ion beam could pertain to significant instabilities present during the high voltage phase in the POS.

articleTitle: Application of the high power charged particle beams in dynamical physics of high pressures
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Application of powerful particle beams for generation of extreme states of matter has a set of serious advantages of other traditional experimental techniques. Appropriate machines are developed now for problems of inertial fusion. Along with putting into operation they can be explored in dynamical experiments for extension of dynamical methods to a new range of high pressures and temperatures.

articleTitle: Observation of high-power microwave radiation from an intense relat1vistic electron beam-plasma system
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High-power microwave radiation was observed from interactions of an intense relativistic electron beam (IREB) with an unmagnetized axially decaying plasma, using a 5-channel microwave spectrometer covering a frequency range from 18 GHz to 40 GHz. The maximum plasma frequency in the drift tube was nearly equal to or less than 18 GHz. Microwave spectra, which were measured both radially and axially, were broad, and the powers had a tendency to increase with frequency.

articleTitle: Restriction of radiation pulse duration in microwave generators using microsecond REB
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Single mode generation with 3 cm wave-lenghth, 300 ns pulse duration,microwave power 50 MW was obtained. Duration of the microwave pulse was less than that of the beam current pulse. The reason for the pulse duration limitation is the increasing of the beam radius in time.

articleTitle: Collective ion acceleration by a modulated microsecond REB
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A two-stage scheme of ion collective acceleration is investigated on the basis of simultaneous space and time modulation of the REB.
