At the first stage the REB time modulation is realized via ions accelerated by a virtual cathode (VC) field. At the second stage, the REB modulated at a frequency of about 20MHz, is injected to the drift chamber placed in the space-periodic magnetic field, where space modulation of the beam takes place. In the drift. chamber, the ions from the VC are accelerated by a slow travelling wave of REB

articleTitle: Computer simulation of explosive electron emission initiation processes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The generalized model is suggested for the physical processes while the convert ion of the field emission into explosive emission of electrons, accompanied by abrupt destruction of the emitter and the intensive dispersion of its material. The complex of the phenomena is considered, allowing for nonstationarity and spatial inhomogeneity of the correlated electromagnetic, thermal and gasdynamic processes, as well as the peculiarities of the thermal properties of the substances arising under considered conditions. Numerical analysis of the electric explosional processes is carried out and the discussion of the obtained results is accomplished.

articleTitle: Progress in the development of a high power focussing B-applied extractor type ion diode for the 1.5 TW pulse generator KALIF
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report on the development of a high power focussing B-applied extractor type ion diode for the 1.5 TW pulse generator KALIF. Using a Ti-Pd metal hydride film on the anode surface and diverting part of the generator current through the anode film with the help of plasma opening switches a hydrogen plasma is preformed on the anode before any voltage is applied to the diode gap. Ion efficiencies of up to 95% are achieved if a strong insulating magnetic field is applied. Thereby it is possible to generate up to 0.7 TW ion power in the diode of which approximately 90% is in protons.

articleTitle: Focusing of intense ion beam by the “Inverse Pinch Ion Diode”
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Focusing of intense ion beams has been attained with the “Inverse Pinch Ion Diode” which has a flat anode. The energy of the ion beam was 180 keV. At the focal point, the ion current density of 0.5 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has been obtained and the focusing radius of the ion beam (FWHM) is 10 mm. Focusing of the ion beam is due to the electrostatic field in the “Inverse Pinch Ion Diode”.

articleTitle: Plasma-anode ion diode research at Cornell: Repetitive-pulse, and 0.1 TW single-pulse experiments
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The magnetized anode plasma (MAP) ion source for magnetically-insulated ion diodes was shown in the LONG-SHOT experiment<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1)</sup> to have some significant advantages over standard “flashboard” anodes. A second generation of MAP diodes is being developed in two experiments: RRID, a high repetition-rate ion diode and a diode to run at 500kV, ~0.1 TW on the Neptune 3Ω pulse line. In both experiments, improved preionization of the gas puff which forms the anode plasma has proved critical for reproducible operation. RRID is now investigating the limits on rep.-rate approaching 1kHz, and Neptune will test the scaling of ion current density usable pulse length and beam optics to higher power pulses.

articleTitle: The optimization of the roentgen radiation converters of high power electron beams
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The calculation results of the integral and differential characteristics of roentgen radiation converter fields for various materials (molybdenum, tantalum) and forms (a standards many foils variants in a transversal magnetic field) in the energy range of incident electrons to 10 MeV are presented. The calcularions were performed using the Monte-Carlo programme based on the model of large collisions taking into account the bremsstrahlung and characteristic K-series radiations as well as on the algorithm of the solution of the relativistic equation of electron motion in the integral gaps. The obtained results allow the converter thickness to be optimized over the total output energy of roentgen radiation and over produced surface absorbed dose in various materials (water, silicon, gold). The gain in radiated energy and dose was obtained at the expense of more effective radiation output and a softer energy spectrum.

articleTitle: Dynamics of stress waves and temperature fields in metals at high-current pulsed electron beam irradiation
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The report presents some results of theoretical and experimental investigation of the temperature fields and stress waves appearing in metals under the influence of high-current pulsed electron beams irradiation. As a result the relation has been established of the temperature field configuration and dynamics to the electron beam parameters. Excitation mechanisms and evolution of stress waves spreading from the irradiated surface into the sample bulk have also been studied.

articleTitle: Microwave generation by the relativistic Cherenkov devices
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report some results of the Cherenkov relativistic devices investigations, namely: theory of dielectric Cherenkov maser (DCM), experiments on twystron and magnetrons.

articleTitle: High power microwave tubes for scientific instrumentation
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Particle accelerators, thermonuclear fusion machines, such as Tokamaks, and many free electron lasers are currently using high CW or pulsed power microwave tubes. We will briefly describe the characteristics of these tubes, but will point out the technical reasons why much better performances cannot be obtained. These reasons have several origins: heat transfer and cooling (cavities, windows, collectors), cathodes (current loading), breakdown or arcing (DC and RF). However, for the future machines now under consideration, output power requiremenst are at least one order of magnitude above: 1 GW peak for 50 nanoseconds in X-band, 1 or several MW CW in C-band... Several technical innovations have been recently introduced, to reach these goals. But also some fundamental principles have to be slightly modified or even changed.

articleTitle: Cold liquid emitter in charged particles sources
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Possibilities due to use of new type-of emitters, based on the dielectric liquids (different alcohols, technical oils) in the charged particles source are being considered. The results of the experiments on obtaining the pulsed (20-400 μs duration) ion and electron beams with current density, ~10A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> are given.

articleTitle: Plasma filled diode operation with plasma created in situ by a low pressure hollow gas discharge
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Plasma filled diode experiments have been performed at .1 to .5 TW by producing a hollow, Penning like, discharge in low pressure gas inside the A-K gap of an electron beam diode. A low impedance phase was observed whose duration could be controlled by the gas pressure and the initial plasma current. At the end of this low impedance phase, the diode voltage and impedance rise abruptly with observed switching times less than 10 ns.

articleTitle: Influence of collector ions on operation of magnetically insulated diode
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In MID ions, emitted by collector and forming as a result of ionization of the residual gas by electron beam, are focused into the cathode plasma region This effect can negatively influence on diode operation in microsecond range of pulse duration.

articleTitle: The limitation of the ion current density in high power magnetically insulated diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: It follows from the equilibrium equation that ion current density in the magnetically insulated diode (MID) is limited by the finite value of magnetic field near anode. From this point of view some models of MID with different assumptions about electron flow are analysed and comparison with other theories is given. The results of numerical simulation of MID with different electron distributions are given. It is found that the ratio of anode and cathode magnetic fields is limited from above by l<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A</sub> = 1+eUA/mc<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the model of slightly scattering electrons. The numerical simulation of H-field topology changing is carried out.

articleTitle: The interaction of a modulated REB with an inhomogeneous collisional plasma and particle acceleration in plasma dielectric structure-induced fields
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Theoretical and experimental investigations of a modulated REB (2 MeV, 1 A, 2 µs) interaction with a neutral gas of pressure 1–700 Torr are presented. Effective beam-plasma interaction is observed when the plasma frequency is equal to the beam modulation frequency. The wake-field value in the plasma-dielectric structure excited by the electron beam propagating in the plasma channel is also calculated.

articleTitle: Experimental study op shook waves excited by a high-power REB in transparent dielectric media
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental results of the plane shock waves, excited by a high-power REB with recording their propogation velocities are described.

articleTitle: Production of tightly focused ion beam and beam-target interaction by “Plasma Focus Diode”
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A high-bright, self-magnetically insulated, coaxial ion-beam diode, “Plasma Focus Diode” (PFD), was used to generate a tightly focused ion beam. A calculation model is developed for PFD and the calculated results are compared with previously reported experimental results. With the ion-beam power density of ~ 0.1 TW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the proton energy loss in aluminium target is studied both experimentally and theoretically. The enhanced energy deposition is observed and is found to be understandable by considering the temperature effect in target plasma.

articleTitle: Utilization of hybrid plasma structures in electron UHF devices
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Hybrid plasma slowing structures are offered for utilization in electron UHF devices. Advantages of such devices in comparison with vacuum and purely plasma those are discussed and the estimation of conditions providing the achievement of hybrid properties in them is carried out.

articleTitle: Experimental and theoretical investigations of generation of electromagnetic emission in the vircators
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Present paper represents the results of theoretical and experimental in - vestigation on studying a generation mechanism and improving a radiation efficiency in a virtual cathode triode. It shows the possibility to produce a new type of a high-frequency monochromatic radiation generator with a frequency tuned.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on the conduction phase of the microsecond plasma opening switch
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of the experimental studies on the conduction phase of the microsecond plasma opening switch are given. It was shown that during this phase the translation of current channel (CC) in the plasma near the anode was taking place with anomalous high velocity. The ion component of the current reached 25–30% of the total value, and the current lines late in the conduction phase acquired considerable slant in the axial direction. The ion current behind the CC made up more than 30% of the total current there; the ion current density reached the maximum already in the conduction phase and slowly decreased during switching.

articleTitle: Simulation of the magnetically self insulated multimodule systems
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The MITL-based multimodule system simulation results are presented. The effects connected with pulse beginning times variations are under consideration. There are some difference may exists in the values of the currents at the beginning and at the end of the long MITL. The example is given when the current at the end of line more than the current at the beginning by 20%.

articleTitle: Exploding metal film active anode source experiments on the lion extractor ion diode
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Exploding metal film anode plasma source (EM-FAAPS) experiments have shown that intense beams with improved turn-on time compared to epoxy-filled-groove anodes can be produced. When a plasma opening switch is used to provide the current path that explodes the thin film anode the ion turn-on time is reduced by about 5ns compared with the previous scheme in which an electron collector on the anode provided this current, and by 10ns compared to epoxy anodes.

articleTitle: Study of HF plasma turbulence excited by REB
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of investigation of HF turbulent plasma oscillations, excited by a powerful relativistic electron beam in the plasma column placed in a longitudinal magnetic field are presented. The observation of the pulsed CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-laser radiation scattered by plasma oscillations at the angles α = 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>÷2·10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> rad is the main diagnostic method. A five-channel system of the scattered radiation recording provides information on the frequency and wave number spectrum of the turbulence during a pulse. Two additional diagnostic methods are used. The first one is a studying of hydrogen lines Stark profiles. The second one is an observation of plasma frequency harmonics in a submillimeter spectral range.

articleTitle: The development and application of charged particle high power beam accelerators in Nuclear Physics Institute, Tomsk
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The parameters and the characteristics of charged particle high power beam accelerators developed in the Tomsk Nuclear Physics Institute are presented, as well as the results of their application to generate high power microwave radiation and to perform investigations in material science.

articleTitle: Study on ablation of target material irradiated by 0.lGW/cm2 pulsed proton beams
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The process of ablation due to irradiation of medium power pulsed ion beams is investigated using a “collector-RES method” together with a charged-particle detection method. The ablation mass and angular distribution are evaluated as a function of the ion current density and the target material. To eliminate the carbon contamination of the beam, an independent trial is made to deflect the neutralized ion beams by a “momentum filter” using a transverse magnetic field. It is shown that the measured focus points agree well with those calculated under the assumption of no electric field, although the ion current density is high enough for the polarization electric field to hinder the ions from being deflected.

articleTitle: Operating characteristics of a high power X-band gyroklystron
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: At the University of Maryland we have designed<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>) and are operating a high power two-cavity TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</sub> gyroklystron in the 9.7-10.0 GHz range. The target beam power is derived from a 500 kV beam with a current ranging from 120-240 A in 1 μs pulses. The target microwave parameters for this tube include a power level of 15-30 MW with a gain of 25-30 dB. In this paper we describe the initial characterization of the electron gun performance and detail preliminary microwave amplifier experiments. We also discuss modifications recently made to the two cavity circuit to improve stability.

articleTitle: Design features of megavolt generators for production of microsecond E-beams with energy more than 100 kJ
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High-power microsecond REBs have the using for plasma heating in solenoidal magnetic systems. In this connection the accelerators U-1, U-2 and U-3 have been designed and constructed at Institute of Nuclear Physics. These accelerators are based on high-voltage pulse generators of the voltage about 1 MV. The pulse generators of the U-1 and U-2 devices are the LC-type Fitch's scheme. The high-voltage generator U-3 operates as a capacitor storage charged by a special cascade source. There was chosen an open-air designing variant of the generators with a multifilm insulation.

articleTitle: Experiments on high power ion beam generation in self insulated diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The experimental results on High Power Ion Beams (HPIB) generation in vacuum spherical focusing diode with self magnetic insulation, which was established on nanosecond accelerator P.A.RUS of 0.2 TW power and 60 ns pulse duration (with matched load) are given. The application of coaxial Plasma Opening Switch (POS) prior to the diode resulted in the factor of 1.8 increase of the diode power in comparison with matched operation without POS.

articleTitle: Ion divergence and the stability of magnetically insulated diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Cold fluid equilibria for magnetically insulated ion diodes are unstable<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>). The interaction of these unstable waves with electrons leads to loss above a threshold wave amplitude<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The waves also interact with ions producing both divergence and energy spread. The magnitude of these effects depends strongly on the diode equilibrium and the wave parameters. Since, previous stability analyses ignored the virtual cathode and the charge-neutral region, both important features of Applied-B ion diode equilibria<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>), we have investigated diode stability with these features included. The nature of ion diode instability is changed dramatically. Ultimately one would like to control ion divergence and energy spread, which depend on the wave amplitudes. We present test particle calculations of wave-electron interactions within the diode. Comparison of our results with 3-D PIC simulations<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>), indicate that wave amplitudes late in the simulations are just large enough to produce electron loss. This suggests that a reduction in ion divergence might result from decreasing the wave amplitude required to induce electron loss. This and other possible approaches for reducing ion divergence are discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization of self-magnetically insulated “Plasma Focus Diode” on KALIF
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Self-magnetically insulated “Plasma Focus Diode” (PFD) successfully developed at Nagaoka has been installed on KALIF, where efforts were carried out to clarify basic characteristics as well as to optimize the ion beam extracted. Various combination of anode and cathode has been studied to obtain best matching of PFD with KALIF. Characteristics of PFD have been found strongly dependent on the factor of g expressed by g = (ln(r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>/r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>))<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, where r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub> and r<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> is the radious of anode and cathode, respectively. The impedance increases with increasing 1/g. At 1/g <; 0.3, it decreases rapidly. The power delivered to PFD achieves the maximum at 1/g ~ 0.3. At 1/g >; 0.3, good focusing takes place where both divergence angle and focusing radius are small, whereas focusing becomes worse at 1/g <; 0.3. From the above studies, we have found the best performance of PFD with KALIF is obtained at 1/g = 0.3 ~ 0.35.

articleTitle: Dynamics of a long-pulsed electron beam under transport in the low-density gas
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results of the studies of the pulsed electron beam transport (E=300 keV, I=10-50 A, τ=10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> s-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> s) in a long channel (L=22.5 m, Ø=0.1 m) under the gas pressure 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-4</sup> Torr are given. The obtained spatial and time dependence of the current transported in a long channel with and without the external focusing system are discussed.

articleTitle: Numerical investigation of the hydrodynamical evolution of the matter under intensive impulse actions
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Present paper is dedicated to the two-dimensional mathematical simulation of the strong shock waves generation processes, accompanied by transition of matter into the extremal state, a plasma corona formation. thus leading to the destruction of a metal barriers under intensive impact action on them by the concentrated energy streams (CES: micrometeorites, high power ion beams - PIB).

articleTitle: Radiation effect on pellet implosion in LIB ICF
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper the radiation transport effect on pellet implosion is studied in a Light-Ion-Beam(LIB) inertial Confinement Fusion(ICF) by numerical simulation and analyses. First we present the nonuniformity-smoothing effect of the radiation transport on an implosion symmetry of the LIB-ICF fuel pellet. Then the radiation effect on the Rayleigh-Taylor instability is studied. The numerical studies present the following results: The 2-dimensional implosion simulation shows that the initial nonuniformity can be smoothed out well in a LIB ICF pellet in which the electron temperature is low, for example several hundreds eV, compared with that in a Laser fusion; For example the initial nonuniformity of 6% is smoothed down to 0.07% during the implosion phase. In addition, the linear analyses for the Rayleigh-Taylor instability shows the damping effect of the radiation transport.

articleTitle: High frequency, high power microwave generation with the “Point Pinch Diode”
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: High-frequency, high-power microwave radiations by a virtual cathode oscillator have been observed with the “Point Pinch Diode” which can produce higher beam density of electrons. The peak power of microwave pulses is typically 350 MW at the frequency region of 20-22 GHz. The radiation frequency increases almost linearly from 22 to 35 GHz with decreasing anode-cathode gap spacing. The mechanism for microwave emission is ascribed to the oscillation of the virtual cathode.

articleTitle: The IRES Generator for the research of material processing and modification
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The Intense Relativistic Electron Beam Generator (IREBG) for the research of material processing and modification is described in this paper. The Marx generator is constructed by using 41 modules of ceramic capacitors and 21 pairs of spark gaps. The Pulse — Forming Network is Blumlein Transmission Line (BTL) filling up with transformer oil. The main switch is four spark gaps self-breakdown switch. Three channel sparks of main switch discharge are obtained because the irradiation coming from discharge of the gap between Marx generator output and BTL. To take the sulphate of copper resistor 38Ω as equivalent load, the output parameters of lREBG are voltage about 400KV, current about 10KA, pulse width about 15ns, rise - time of output voltage less than 4ns. The experiment on the electron beam diode and X — ray tube as real loads will be soon made in our Lab.

articleTitle: The Microsecond Plasma Current Interrupting Switch
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental results of Microsecond Plasma Current Interrupting Switch (PCIS) investigations are reported in the paper. Basic PCIS parameters are determined and operating mechanism is investigated. Recommendations for PCIS usage in high power multi-MJ generators are given.

articleTitle: Intense beams of highly-ionized metallic ions generated in the “Point Pinch Diode”
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Although the input energy to diodes was about 1 kJ, the “Point Pinch Diode” could produce an intense flux of ion beams up to 90 kA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Significant fraction of metallic ion beams of anode materials was also detected and when heavier metallic anodes were employed, highly-ionized metallic ions were generated.

articleTitle: Lithium beam experiments at 425 kV
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experiments on the interactions of a Lithium ion beam with a dense hydrogen plasma channel will be discussed. The 550kV ion beam is generated by a magnetically insulated race track diode. Using a sequence of in situ anode heating and discharge cleaning a very pure (approximately 90%) Lithium beam is produced. This beam is passed through a set of apertures and an energy selector before it is injected into the plasma channel. The plasma channel is 71cm in length and is produced by discharging a 25kJ capacitor bank into a theta-pinch coil. The plasma density varies from 1-5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> as measured by a holographic interferometer and the plasma temperature is determined by spectroscopy to be around 20 eV. The exiting beam particles are analysed by a Thomson parabola to determine the ionization state of the Lithium. Of particular interest are the charge changing interactions whereby Li<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and Li<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">++</sup> interact with plasma protons to become Li<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">++</sup> and Li<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+++</sup>.

articleTitle: A program of high power microwave source research and development from 8 GHz to 600 GHz
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We review research results both on a plasma filled, backward wave oscillator (BWO), and on a free electron laser (FEL) driven by a sheet electron beam. Recently, it was demonstrated that a plasma filled BWO driven by an intense relativistic electron beam can generate hundreds of megawatts of microwave radiation at an unusually high efficiency of 40% compared with a typical efficiency of ∼10% in a BWO without a background plasma. Furthermore, the enhanced efficiency can be maintained even for large electron beam currents approaching the vacuum space charge limiting current, and we anticipate this might hold even for larger current values. Theoretical studies and numerical simulations indicate that the enhanced efficiency as well as a lower value for the start oscillation current in the linear regime may be due to the finite length of the BWO circuit coupled with modification of the dispersion relation due to the background plasma. In the case of our FEL studies, we present designs for a 1 MW, CW, tapered FEL amplifier operating at frequencies of 280 GHz and 560 GHz. A short wiggler period (ℓ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf> ∼ 1 cm) is combined with a sheet beam of electrons having energy ∼ 1 MeV. Depressed collector techniques would allow the main power supply rating to be reduced to ∼ 200 kV. Efficient sheet beam transport (> 99%) has been demonstrated through 10 wiggler periods, and transport through 60 wiggler periods is currently under study. Finally, plans for a proof-of-principle tapered FEL amplifier experiment at 94 GHz are presented.

articleTitle: Spectral and angular characteristics of relativistic vircator radiation
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The paper deals with the spectral and angular characteristics of a relativistic vircator. In a relativistic case the radiation is shown to be concentrated on surfaces of two cones with the angle of 2θ~mc<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/E near the plane of oscillating electrons. In this case the total radiation power is W~ (E/mc<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and a maximum of radiation is at the first harmonics in the spectrum.

articleTitle: Theoretical investigation of intense electron beam interaction with target in high current diode
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The interaction of pinched relativistic electron beam with a thin bremsstrahlung target is calculated by use of the Monte Carlo method for energy deposition and two-dimensional particle- in-cell hydrodynamics to take into account the effects of target expansion and magnetic field penetration. It is found that bremsstrahlung efficiency increasing, converter optimum thickness decreasing and bremsstrahlung spectrum softering occur due to magnetic stopping in low density target. The automodel solution of plasma motion is considered.

articleTitle: Rayleigh-Taylor instability in LIB ICF
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The Rayleigh-Taylor(R-T) Instability is one of the problems in the Light-Ion-Beam(LIB) Inertial-Confinement-Fusion (ICF)-pellet. The nonuniform acceleration field and the radiation effects on the LIB-ICF-pellet implosion to the high density are investigated by the linear analyses in this paper. By means of these analyses we obtained the following two results: 1) The nonuniform acceleration field in space does not change the growth rate(γ) of the R-T instability. However this nonuniformity may suppress the R-T instability in some particular cases. 2) The radiation may reduce the growth rate(γ).

articleTitle: The influence of microwave radiation of relativistic generator on magnetic susceptibility of HTSC ceramics
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The investigation of the influence of the pulse microwave radiation of relativistic generator on the magnetic characteristic of HTSC ceramics was carried out and it was shown that within the certain interval of the absorbed power of microwave radiation the improvement of the critical parameters of superconductor is observed.

articleTitle: Multiple beam induction linac research at LBL
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We present results of progress on the LBL multiple beam induction linac experiment (MBE-4). This machine models the accelerator physics of the electric-focused portion of a driver for heavy ion inertial confinement fusion. Four beams of cesium ions are accelerated in common through twenty four induction gaps while being separately focussed in individual electrostatic AG focussing channels. Early experiments have demonstrated current amplification in the linac, from 10 mA to 90 mA per beam. This is achieved both by acceleration (from 200 keV to 1 MeV) and by carefully controlled bunch compression. Recent experiments have concentrated on studies of beams extracted from an ion source which produces 5 mA cesium beams at emittances near 0.03 π mm-mrad (normalized). Experiments and theory show a growth of emittance (by about a factor of 2) as these beams are accelerated through the linac. Results of recent measurements of the transverse emittance behavior of these strongly space-charge-dominated ion beams are reviewed and compared with theory.

articleTitle: Axially resolved PEOS measurements at microsecond conduction times
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Plasma erosion opening switch conduction phase studies. at microsecond conduction times and both 200 and 800 kA current levels, are reported here. Similar data were obtained from both experiments. A current channel is seen to propagate toward the load, and this channel is associated with an increased ion current and cathode and switch plasma luminosity. There is evidence of local opening during the conduction phase. which may be related to hydrodynamic effects.

articleTitle: Transverse magnetic field effect on the non-mongenergetic REB transport in low pressure gas
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Experimental studies of REB transport in transverse magnetic field at gas pressure from 510<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> to 5 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> Torr. The beam energy in a pulse were stepped from 300 keV to 150 keV. At low pressure each portion of the beam was transported by the individual cyclotron trajectories. At higher pressures the low energy portion of the beam moved in the channel wich had been formed by the first high-energy beam port ion. A theoretical evaluation of the phenomena is proposed.

articleTitle: RF power generation for future linear colliders
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The TeV collider RF source development effort at SLAC is being concentrated on both the high-power conventional klystron followed by some form of RF pulse compression (not necessarily three-stage binary described here) and the CFA. The relativistic klystron provided an excellent experimental source for initial high-gradient accelerator experiments. The induction linac required to make high current relativistic beams for these klystrons appears at present to be too expensive for use in a high pulse rate mode. The 100 MW conventional klystron is promising but requires stable operation at 800 ns with pulse compression to 100 ns. This has yet to be demonstrated. Problems with RF voltage breakdown in cavity gaps, ceramic windows and pulse compression waveguide components must be solved. The CFA development is not as far along as the klystron and will be a serious collider RF source candidate only if stable operation can be achieved above 200 MW. If one of these two approaches emerges as the more feasible, the focus of further effort will be toward producing that source at low cost.

articleTitle: High power vircator research at physics international
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Physics International reports the results of a three-phase program to explore the feasibility of constructing and operating a large array of high power, phase-locked vircators. The approach has been to study multiple high power sources in all the relative configurations that would be encountered in an array architecture. Resonant cavities enclosing the virtual cathodes reduce the bandwidth of the oscillations sufficiently to allow phase-locking. Locking is observed between sources generating microwave powers exceeding 1 GW. It is shown that high power sources can be “over-driven”: strong coupling between sources minimizes the duration of the transient to the locked state, but a limit exists beyond which instabilities defeat phase-locking. The time resolved variation in the final relative phase angle between locked sources and the duration of the transient to the final state both decrease with the initial frequency detuning between the sources.

articleTitle: High current electron beam accelerating module
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: An induction 1 Mev accelerating module was developed to accelerate 100 nsec electron pulses at current of 10 kA. The module is capable to operate in pulse train mode. It comprises of 6 induction cells each supplying 160 kV and driven by 3 hight-voltage impulse generators with mugnetic pulse compression alike the MAG-1 generator. Vacuum spark gaps were used to energy commutation. A process of production metglass cores was developed and the generator cores were made.

articleTitle: Linear induction accelerator of the hollow electron beam
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Short description of the main systems of the holow electron beam linear induction accelerator (LIA) is given. The main characteristic features of the accelerator are; homogeneous solenoidal, pulse guiding magnetic field with strength up to 1.5 T in aperture 120 mm, high beam energy gain 10 keV/cm and beam current up to 1.5 kA; the lack of drift section between the electron sourse and induction system; the use in modulator of one thyratron and three stages of power compression providing power 7.5 GW with pulse duration 60 ns on the load 0.75 Ohm. The LIA characteristics, its possibilities, the measurement procedure of LIA and beam parameters in on-line regime are presented.

articleTitle: Improvement of the E-field triggered surface breakdown of dielectric anodes in vacuum ion diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: To improve the dielectric flashover in adsorbates at the surface of dielectric inserts of vacuum diode anodes, start electrons are implemented by several means. The first method is to trap a layer of electrons at the structured surface (grooves) by means of auxiliary electrodes. A second method uses the idea that a low gap semiconducting surface layer spends electrons into the adsorbates, if the electric field passes a critical value. Experiments with a pinch reflex diode at the 1.2 TW pulse generator `Kalif' will be reported. On the basis of the latter method anode inserts are tested, which are woven from glassfiber. The weak conductivity of glass and the ability to trap a desired amount of adsorbates (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>,He, N<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> for example) makes it possible to form proper plasmas and to do it without hydrocarbon. One of the results of the current investigation is that the micro inhomogeneity of the ion beam could be reduced drastically. A first full-scale test in a B<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Θ</sub>-diode at the PPL `Kalif' is presented.

articleTitle: Present status of FEL research in Japan
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper, three items are presented. Firstly, FEL facilities and results in Japan are summarized. Secondary, RF Linac-FEL project for industrial applications are reviewed. Thirdly FEL application for inertial confinement fusion is discussed.

articleTitle: The formation of high current particle flows in systems with plasma opening switch
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The performance of a plasma opening switch (POS) has been studied experimentally using a ns pulsed power generator and also a small coaxial test setup. The results were obtained for the oases when the plasma was injected either from the outer or from the inner electrode. It has been shown that one of the features of the POS action is the generation of high current particle flows.

articleTitle: Thermoemission gun with high magnetic compression of a hollow microsecond 400 keV, 400 A electron beam
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A thermoemission gun is realized to form a hollow intense relativistic electron beam with the current 400 A and the energy of electrons 400 keV. The external diameter and the thickness of the beam in the drift channel are 20 mm and 2.5 mm, respectively.

articleTitle: Method of intense magnetized REB production with large transverse velocities
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The method for production of a beam with electron pith-angles of about unity, but with a small angular spread is suggested. The method is based on the sharp change of the magnetic line of force direction. The possibilities of experimental realization of this method at GOL-3 device are discussed.

articleTitle: A single-mode operation of Plasma Cherenkov Maser (PCM)
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The first operation of a plasma maser /1/, utilizing High-Current REB showed the possibility of Cherenkov radiation of intense microwaves from plasma waveguides and therefore the possibility of constructing single-mode High - Power microwave generators using REB. The parameters of the Plasma Cherenkov Maser such as threshold plasma density, startup current of the utilized relativistic electron beam (REB), efficiency and gain were calculated in the high magnetic field limit in previous works /2,3,4/. The estimate conditions of beam kinetic energy transform into a plasma coaxial waveguide TEM mode were analyzed in /2/. By now we have developed this project and improved the quality and mode composition of the output microwave power. We'll discuss two groups of new experimental results corresponding to various geometries of the PCM.

articleTitle: “VIVA- I”, versatile inductive voltage adder for high-voltage pulse-power generation
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Versatile inductive voltage adder system, “VIVA-I”, with high potential gradient has been successfully developed. It has been designed to produce output pulse of 4 MV, 60 ns by adding 2 MV pulses in 2-stages of induction cells, where amorphous cores are installed. Within ~40 % of full charge voltage, pulse-power characteristics of Marx generator, pulse-forming line (PFL) , transmission line, and induction cells were tested for three types of load; open circuit, dummy load of CuSO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> resistor, and electron diode. In open circuit test, ~2.0 MV of output voltage was obtained with good reproducebility. Dependence of output voltage on diode impedance was evaluated by using a dummy load, and good agreement was obtained with that expected. An E-beam diode was operated successfully, and 18 kA of beam current was obtained.

articleTitle: Resonant laser diagnostics of intense pulsed ion diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Laser-based diagnostic methods are developed to improve our understanding of the behavior of flashover-type magnetically-insulated diodes. For the quantitative estimation of the particle density, a resonant interferometric and a laser resonance scattering method are developed. These techniques could allow direct determination of the particle distribution in the diode gap. A new diode which uses actively produced source plasma is tested for the investigation of the anode plasma effect on the diode characteristics.

articleTitle: High poyer U-2 generator of long pulse ribbon REBS
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: One of the promising ways to heat plasma in the open solenoidal systems as GOL-3 device<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1)</sup>, is to use relativistic electron beams with a ribbon cross section<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2)</sup>. These beams should be generated in the foilless ribbon diodes which can produce at 1 MV voltage the electron current about 50–100 kA with pulse duration at least 10µs<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The electron beam generated in this diode may have a small angular spread at the moderate (0.5–1. OT) magnetic field<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3)</sup> and this fact is very important for beam plasma interaction. In addition the ribbon electron beams may be switched into the same magnetic flux tube by the reconnection of the guiding magnetic field lines that opens the way of the further increase of the beam energy content<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4)</sup>. According to these motivations U-2 generator of the ribbon REB is constructed at our Institute as E-beam injector of GOL-3 device<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2)</sup>.

articleTitle: The excitation of the fundamental mode of a coaxial plasma slow-wave structure of a PCM-amplifier
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The present work is devoted to the experimental investigation of high-power microwave radiation transport down an overmoded co axial plasma waveguide meeting the condition of eXCitation of aZimuthally symmetric modes. This is the first step in constructing a PCM (Plasma Cherenkov Maser)-amplifier, driven by a high-current relativistic electron beam (REB).

articleTitle: Progress in investigations on a dense plasma compression on “Angara-5-1”
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The results on implosion of multishell liners in the “Angara-5-1” accelerator diode at currents to 3.5 MA were presented. Radiation growth fronts t ~ 3 nsec and the interval shell temperature of 100 eV were obtained. The formation of Z-pinches from continuous and porous media was studied. The new module scheme with p>;6-8 W to modernize the “A-5-1” facility is discussed.

articleTitle: µm electron beam generation in the diodes with explosive cathodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Vacuum planar diodes with explosive emitting cathodes for microsecond electron beam generation are discussed. Cathodes with current reduce resistors in the circuit of cathode plasma initiators and low electric strength of the cathode plasma initiators are described. The current yield of the beam and surface hardening of instrumental steel by low energy electron beam research results are presented.

articleTitle: Temporal characterization of the 19-MV, 700-kA HERMES III electron beam
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The shot-to-shot variation of the HERMES III Accelerator parameters at the electron-beam diode, the time dependence of the electron flow in the diode, and the time dependence of the subsequent radiation produced from the bremsstrahlung target are measured and compared with model results. The measurements are made with current shunts, H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup> range filters, a calorimeter, a fast-framing γ-ray camera, and Compton diodes. The measurements show that the peak voltage and energy delivered to the target are 19±0.2 (±2) MV and 327±6 (±60) kJ, respectively; the electron beam converges to a radius of 14.0±0.3 cm near peak power; and the FWHM of the radiation pulse varies from 14.5±0.9 ns at the radiation focus to 23.6±0.9 ns in the far field. (The errors not in parentheses correspond to the RMS shot-to-shot variation. Those in parentheses correspond to the estimated systematic uncertainty.) The measurements agree with the calculated shot-variability and the dynamics of the electron flow, and suggest that the model can be used to predict the response from similar multi-stage, coaxial, high-power accelerators. With over 1000 shots accumulated between the commissioning of HERMES III and the present set of measurements, no degradation of output has been observed.

articleTitle: Physical principles of plasma opening switch operation and the choice of theory
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Studies on the theory of a plasma opening switch are briefly surveyed, the method of choosing the theory appropriate for this device is proposed. Results of the theory of ion current transfer in a cylindrical plasma switch are presented.

articleTitle: Magnetic compression of an aluminium vapor cylinder
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Z-pinch is obtained with a supersonic aluminium metal vapor jet as a load for a 0.1 TW pulsed power machine G.A.E.L. A 8∶1 compression has been obtained with a large X-ray emission in the aluminium K-shell. A large number of diagnostics are used to characterize the plasma.

articleTitle: Measurements of hydrogen line profiles in the REBEX experiment
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report our measurements of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</sub> line profile by both the time resolved emission spectroscopy and the over the laser pulse (5 μs) integrated intracavity laser spectroscopy. It was found that during REB-plasma interaction neutral particles are excited and heated surprisingly fast and the Doppler effect masks all other broadening mechanisms.

articleTitle: High-current RF ion accelerators with longitudinal magnetic field focusing
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The development of ion linacs with superconducting solenoid focusing IS underway to increase the beam current. An experimental proton linac has been constructed, the 1. 5-MeV, 0.4-A beam has been obtained. A conceptual design of a cw accelerator that may be used for current drive in ITER is presented.

articleTitle: Model for calculation of output characteristics of nanosecond reb generator with Plasma Opening Switch
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: A model for the output characteristics calculation of a powerful relativistic electron beams generator with Plasma Opening Switch (POS) is presented. The model is based on the consideration of an installation output assembly, including POS, as vacuum lines with magnetic self-insulation. Using this analogy current losses during the pulse passage in line with POS are explained by an inconsistency on the diode border of plasma and in the region adjacent to diode. The model proposed allows to calculate these losses.

articleTitle: Superpower pulsed systems with plasma opening switches
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: In this paper the development and application of terawatt pulsed power generators with intermediate inductive energy store and microsecond plasma opening switches shall be reported.

articleTitle: Beam - plasma ionization processes at low gas pressure
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report the investigation stationary plasma density profiles in a beam-plasma interaction. The plasma parameters and the beam - plasma discharge criterion are determined.

articleTitle: Some POS operating regimes on the GIT-4 generator
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report the experimental results performed to clear the possible ways for POS performance improvement. Those are two: 1) the increase of the magnetic field on the POS anode structure. and 2) the increase of the current rise rate in second POS stage with a deminished cathode electrode diameter.

articleTitle: Plasmodynamic effects for magnetically insulated systems
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Results of investigation of surface plasma. produced by electrical explosion of electrods of current concentrator. are presented. Experiments were performed at a current I = 3-4 MA. dI/dt ~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> A/s. Solid (CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub>. (CD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sub> or foam agar-agar were used as material of cylindrical loads. An investigation of spatial and temporary characteristics of soft X-ray radiation and laser measurements were performed to study both the dense plasma in a neck of Z-pinch and the comparatively rare plasma in periphery of pinch. An analysis of influence of this plasma on neck's parameters is presented.

articleTitle: Nonlinear dynamics of REB interaction with slow waves of plasma periodical structures
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: We report the main results of a theoretical study on the excitation of coupled plasma and electromagnetic waves by relativistic electron beams. Investigated is the case of a parametric coupling between the electromagnetic and plasma waves by a periodical rippling of a conducting screen. We also present the analysis of irregular dynamics in coupled BWO.

articleTitle: Electron beam in a two-turn stellatron
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: The motion of the reference electrons and the equilibrium of the relativistic electron are investigated in the magnetic field configuration of a two-turn stellatron. Electron trajectories are found with the eddy electric field taken into account. The beam density distribution is also derived.

articleTitle: Neutron bursts from a dense Z-pinch discharge
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Neutron production process in a high density Z-discharge formed with a small deuterated organic fiber was investigated. The Z-pinch discharge, which was self-crowbared at about peak current was driven with a pulse power generator. The neutron yield strongly depended on the load current but exhibited a weak dependence on the fiber diameter and length. As soon as abrupt current decrease, neutron burst, which consisted of fine structures, was observed and sometimes it had a double pulse structure. The onset time of the second burst increased almost linearly with the initial fiber diameter.

articleTitle: Recent progress of intense pulsed ion-beam driven fusion studies at Nagaoka
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Very tightly-focused ion beam was obtained by “Plasma Focus Diode” (PFD), yielding focusing diameter of ~360 μm, and power density of ~ 0.1 TW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> at the beam energy of ~1.5 MeV. Enhanced energy deposition was observed in the interaction with aluminium target with the enhancement ratio of ~1.5. In comparison of the experimental data with 1-D hydrocode simulation, good agreement is obtained between them. Versatile inductive voltage adder, "VIVA-I", has been successfully developed, which has the pulse-power output of 4 MV, 80 kA, 65 ns. Furthermore, systematic studies are carried out on high frequency response of various saturable cores (ferrite and amorphous) for applications to pulse-power technology. Cylindrical, magnetically insulated ion diode was sucessfully developed, which has the actual cathode rather than virtual cathode to stabilize electric field. Highly repetitive, discharge-pumped, XeCl excimer laser is developed with subsonic gas flow by using Ludwieg charge tube. Time-resolved spectroscopic measurement is developed on anode plasma of several ion diodes as well as target plasma.

articleTitle: Theory of applied-B ion diodes
publicationTitle: 1990 8th International Conference on High-Power Particle Beams
abstract: Progress in the development of the theory of applied-B ion diodes has been rapid since the BEAMS'88 meeting. This paper describes recent advances in the analytic theory and numerical simulation of applied-B ion diodes in general and, in particular, the diodes being tested experimentally on PBFA-II at Sandia National Laboratories.
